title: Answer every refusal from the shipping module

blocks.text: An online shop's checkout books a shipment as its last step. The shipping module refuses some orders on purpose, and its team adds new kinds of refusal every few releases without telling the checkout team. Last month one of those new refusals reached the customer as "500 Internal Server Error". The month before, a `NullPointerException` inside the shipping code was shown to customers as "We can't ship this order right now", and nobody was paged for a week.

items: a booked shipment answers with its tracking number;
a postcode the carrier doesn't serve gets `ADDRESS_ANSWER`;
every other refusal from the shipping module, today's and the ones added later, gets `LATER_ANSWER`;
anything else that goes wrong reaches the shop's error handler unchanged.

blocks.text: About six lines in total. The tests bring a refusal of their own that the checkout has never seen.

cases.says: a booked shipment returns its tracking number to the customer
a known refusal other than a bad postcode gets the 'we'll email you' answer
a refusal type the shipping module adds later is answered without changing the checkout
a NullPointerException from a bug in shipping is not turned into a customer answer
the one refusal the checkout treats differently still gets its own answer

origin.section: Give a Module One Base Exception, So Each Caller Chooses How Finely It Catches

concepts: With one base exception per module, a caller that catches a leaf it treats specially and the base for the rest handles a leaf added later without any change.
Catching Exception or RuntimeException instead of the module's base also turns a bug's NullPointerException into a business answer.
